Users using the latest version of Claude Code on macOS and Linux operating systems can now have different sessions send messages to each other to share results, ask questions, and coordinate work. Here are the details.

Claude Code adds cross-session messaging feature

Anthropic announced a new feature earlier today that will be very useful for users who are accustomed to running multiple Claude Code sessions simultaneously.

Starting from Claude Code v2.1.224, different sessions can send messages to each other, sharing progress updates and other relevant information; this feature is particularly useful when users are handling different parts of the same project across multiple sessions.

The following is Anthropic's documentation for this new feature:

Anthropic stated that the best use cases for this new feature include: handing over a finding, coordinating parallel work branches, getting the status of long-running tasks, and replying to messages across computers.

The company further pointed out that users do not need to worry about drafting message content. Users only need to provide the content they wish to convey in the prompt, and Claude will automatically compose the actual message.

It is worth noting that the cross-session messaging feature cannot be used to approve permission requests or change settings. For example, commands such as /compact will be presented as plain text and will not be executed as actual commands; if handling the message requires permission, the receiving session will still issue an approval prompt to the user.
